title: Gillie Da Kidd on LeBron's Sixers Move: 'What Chip?'
htmlContent:
When LeBron Jameschose Philadelphia this summer, the move sent shockwaves through the NBA. Gillie Da Kidd, the Philly-born rapper and co-host of the "Million Dollaz Worth of Game" podcast, cared about one thing: whether it brings a championship to his city.

Gillie made his expectations for James and the 76ers clear when he spoke with LandonBuford.com recently.

"What chip? I ain't talking about the ones you put in your mouth. I'm talking about the ones you celebrate, with the confetti coming down. What the f— you mean?"

For Gillie, a ring is the only thing that matters. Philadelphia hasn't won an NBA title since 1983, and the four-time champion arrives with the same goal.

Why LeBron Picked Philadelphia

James agreed to a two-year, $8 million deal with Philadelphia on July 24, ending his run with the Los Angeles Lakers. His agent, Klutch Sports CEO Rich Paul, said James was prioritizing "basketball happiness." The Sixers sold their roster as his best chance to win another title.

The recruiting effort was a group project. Tyrese Maxey, a fellow Klutch client who has called James his "big brother," led the charge, with Joel Embiid and Jaylen Brown also making their pitch. James later praised Philadelphia's notoriously demanding fans, saying he respects how much they care about their own teams.

A Retooled Roster After a Painful Exit

The Sixers needed a shake-up. They went 45-37 last season and outlasted the Boston Celtics in seven games in the first round. The eventual champion Knicks then swept them out of the Eastern Conference semifinals.

Philadelphia responded aggressively. On July 1, the team acquired Brown from Boston in a deal that sent Paul George and four draft picks to the Celtics. Three weeks later, James signed. Add Maxey, who averaged 28.3 points and 6.6 assists last season and Embiid, and the Sixers have one of the most talented rosters in the league on paper.

Opening Night at the Garden

The new-look Sixers will be tested right away. Philadelphia opens the season Tuesday night at Madison Square Garden against the defending champion New York Knicks. Tipoff is at 7 p.m. ET on NBC and Peacock.

Before the game, the Knicks will raise their championship banner and receive their rings. New York beat the San Antonio Spurs in five games in the NBA Finals to win its first title in 53 years, and Jalen Brunson was named Finals MVP. It was a dominant run. The Knicks won 15 of their last 16 playoff games and set a record for point differential in a single postseason.

That puts the Sixers in an uncomfortable spot. They'll have to watch their division rival celebrate a title it won partly by sweeping them a few months earlier.

The Knicks Are Now the Team to Beat

The championship settled several long-running debates in New York. The franchise's decision to trade a haul of first-round picks for Mikal Bridges looks justified, and questions about whether Brunson could lead a title team have been answered. Karl-Anthony Towns also put to rest criticism of his toughness with a physical, defense-minded postseason.

But the title brings a new kind of pressure. New York is no longer the underdog chasing a breakthrough; it's the team everyone else in the East is chasing. The conference is deeper than it was a year ago. Boston has a healthy Jayson Tatum. Detroit is coming off a 60-win season, and Cleveland just reached the conference finals. Eight different teams have won the last eight championships, which shows how hard it is to repeat.

Bigger Stakes for Philadelphia

For the Sixers, the opener is only one game out of 82 games. Still, it offers an early look at whether James, Brown, Embiid and Maxey can form a contender together, and whether they can match up with the team that ended their season in May.

Philadelphia fans like Gillie aren't interested in moral victories or a good regular season. They want a parade down Broad Street. As Gillie put it, the only chip that counts is the one that comes with confetti, and Tuesday night at the Garden is Philadelphia's first chance to show it's a real contender.
excerpt: Philly-born rapper and "Million Dollaz Worth of Game" co-host Gillie Da Kidd made his expectations crystal clear after LeBron James signed with the Philadelphia 76ers this summer — a championship, and nothing less, will satisfy the city's fans.
